en: Oṃ, salutation to Janakanandinī. Oṃ, salutation to Lokajananī. Oṃ, salutation to Jayavṛddhidā.
Oṃ, homage to Jayodvāhapriyā.
Oṃ, homage to Rāmā.
Oṃ, homage to Lakṣmī.

Oṃ, salutation to the daughter of Janaka. Oṃ, salutation to her who is adorned with two feet that steal the very essence of the lotus. Oṃ, salutation to her who shines with the exquisite tips of the scales of royal gold and rubies.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose ornaments shine with peaks of mountains variegated with jewels and gold. 10.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose hips are adorned by a girdle that surpasses all other gems and vanquishes all enemies.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is served by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas.

Oṃ, salutation to her who is ever-hurried in protecting the people who have taken refuge in her even once. Oṃ, salutation to her who shines with many moons and suns risen simultaneously. Oṃ, salutation to her whose divine yellow garment flashes like a second lightning bolt.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose compassionate glance bestows the desired fruits of the three aims of life and more.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is graced by lotus-like hands ever intent on granting the four aims of life.
Oṃ, salutation to her who shines in the minds of many yogis devoted to the five great sacrifices.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose full majesty consists of the six political expedients.
Oṃ, salutation to the deity who is the source of the seven principles and so forth. 20.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose nose shines with a mark like the crescent moon of the eighth day.
Oṃ, homage to her who is worshipped with nine enclosures.
Oṃ, homage to her who brings bliss to Rāma. Oṃ, homage to Rāmanāthā.
Oṃ, salutation to her who delights Rāghava;
Oṃ, salutation to her whose state of being is permeated by Rāma;
Oṃ, salutation to her whose sovereign majesty is dependent upon Rāma.
Oṃ, salutation to Rāmottamā. Oṃ, salutation to Rājamukhī. Oṃ, salutation to Rañjitāmodakuntalā. 30.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose abode is divine Sāketa.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is served by divine musical instruments.
Oṃ, salutation to her who rejoices in following Rāma.
Oṃ, salutations to her who has made Citrakūṭa her abode.
Oṃ, salutations to her whose ornaments were fashioned by Anasūyā. Oṃ, salutations to her who dwells within a vast heart.
Oṃ, salutation to her who possesses variegated garlands and ornaments.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is intent on crushing the Virādha. Oṃ, salutation to her who has resorted to the banks of the Pañcavaṭī.
Oṃ, salutation to Khadyotanakulānandā. 40.
Oṃ, salutation to Kharādivadhananditā.
Oṃ, salutation to Māyāmārīcamathanā.
Oṃ, homage to her who possesses a form of illusory human nature. Oṃ, homage to her who surpassed the son of Sumitrā in guile.
Oṃ, homage to her whose splendor surpasses that of the lotus.
Oṃ, salutation to her who has treated the Ten-necked One as if he were a blade of grass.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose mind is intent on providing protection. Oṃ, salutation to her who is delighted by the sight of Hanumān.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is skilled in the play of laughter. Oṃ, salutation to her who is satisfied by the sight of the mudrā. 50.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose life is sealed by the mudrā.
Oṃ, homage to her whose dwelling is the Aśoka grove. Oṃ, homage to her who has rendered the gods free from sorrow. Oṃ, homage to her whose resolve was to burn Laṅkā.
Oṃ, salutation to her who obstructs the siege of Laṅkā. Oṃ, salutation to her who is satisfied by having been purified.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is clothed in beautiful garlands and garments.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is praised by the Lord of Contentment.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose abode is a contented heart.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is to be worshipped by her father-in-law. 60.
Oṃ, salutations to her who is worshipped by the one seated upon the lotus. Oṃ, salutations to her who has attained the eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇiman*.
Oṃ, salutations to her who was reached through the compassion of Vibhīṣaṇa.
Oṃ, homage to her who is grown upon divine flowers!
Oṃ, homage to her who is worshipped by the hosts of celestial beings!
Oṃ, homage to her who resembles the hibiscus flower!
Oṃ, salutation to her who is clothed in divine silken garments.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is seated upon a divine lion-throne.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is adorned with divine ornaments and finery.
Oṃ, homage to the beloved queen consecrated in sovereignty.
70. Oṃ, homage to the divine presiding deity of Ayodhyā.
Oṃ, homage to her whose limbs are anointed with divine perfumes.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is beautiful with divine limbs.
Oṃ, salutation to her whose heart is the fresh butter of the cow.
Oṃ, salutation to her who is worshipped by the hosts of tigers.
Oṃ, homage to her who is richly perfumed with camphor; Oṃ, homage to her whose hair is thick and curled;
Oṃ, homage to her who is perfected by a smile like moonlight.
Oṃ, obeisance to her who wears garments of beautiful gold.
Oṃ, obeisance to the Yoginī. (80) Oṃ, obeisance to the Enchantress.
Oṃ, salutation to Staṃbhinī. Oṃ, salutation to Akhilāṇḍeśvarī. Oṃ, salutation to Śubhā.
Oṃ, obeisance to Gaurī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇī. Oṃ, obeisance to Prīti.
Oṃ, homage to Svāhā. Oṃ, homage to Svadhā.
Oṃ, homage to Śivā. 90.
Oṃ, salutation to the Mother who gives joy to those who take refuge in her.
Oṃ, salutation to Bhāratī. Oṃ, salutation to Vārāhī.
Oṃ, salutation to Vaiṣṇavī.
Oṃ, salutation to Brāhmī. Oṃ, salutation to her who is praised by the Siddhas.
Oṃ, homage to her who dwells upon the six seats.
Oṃ, homage to her whose speech is as sweet as the warbling of the kalakaokila bird. Oṃ, homage to her whose anklets are like the cry of the kalahamsa swan.
Oṃ, homage to her who is adorned with virtues such as patience and tranquility. 100.
Oṃ, homage to the mother of Kandarpa.
Oṃ, homage to her who is worshipped by all the worlds.
Oṃ, salutation to the one beloved by the fragrant *sumana* flower.
Oṃ, salutation to Śyāmalā. Oṃ, salutation to the deity who bestows auspiciousness upon all people.
Oṃ, obeisance to Vasudhāputrī. Oṃ, obeisance to Mātaṅgī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Sītā.
Oṃ, homage to Hemāñjanāyikā.
Oṃ, homage to Sītādevī Mahālakṣmī. 110.
Oṃ, homage to Sakalasāṃrājyalakṣmī.
Oṃ, salutations to the bestower of the desired fruits of devotion.
Oṃ, salutations to the bestower of the eightfold fruits. 113. Thus ends the complete list of one hundred and eight names of Sītā.
